docs.title: 🤖 Agent Foundation Documentation
docs.text:
Opinionated, production-ready LLM Agent deployment with enterprise-grade infrastructure.

This template provides a complete foundation for building and deploying LLM Agents to production. Get automated CI/CD, managed state persistence, custom observability, and proven cloud infrastructure out of the box.

Built for teams who need to move beyond prototypes and ship production AI agents with confidence.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• 🐳 Optimized Docker builds - Multi-stage uv builds; code changes push only a kilobyte-sized layer
  • 🏗️ Automated CI/CD - GitHub Actions + Terraform with smart PR automation
  • 🌎 Multi-environment deployments - Production-grade dev/stage/prod isolation
  • 💾 Database sessions - Cloud SQL Postgres for durable conversation state
  • 🔭 Custom observability - OpenTelemetry with full trace-log correlation
  • 🏰 Hardened Cloud SQL - Private IP only, IAM database auth, enforced TLS and Auth Proxy
  • 🔐 Workload Identity Federation - CI/CD authentication (no service account keys)

docs.title: Development
docs.text: Day-to-day development workflow, code quality, testing, and connecting to deployed resources.

docs.title: Local Development
docs.text:
Start the agent with uv run server. It reads .env (setup: Getting Started) and needs no containers or deployed infrastructure.

SERVE_WEB_INTERFACE=TRUE uv run server                     # API and ADK web UI at 127.0.0.1:8000
SERVE_WEB_INTERFACE=TRUE RELOAD_AGENTS=TRUE uv run server  # Reload the agent on edits under src/
LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG uv run server                              # Debug logging

With the service URIs in .env unset, ADK stores sessions and artifacts locally under src/<package>/.adk/ and keeps memory in-process (Environment Variables: Cloud Resources). .env is shared with Docker Compose: with the URIs set, uv run server uses the deployed services instead, and reaching the session database needs an IAP tunnel: Compose starts one, or start it yourself (Cloud Backend Options).

RELOAD_AGENTS reloads the agent, tools, callbacks and prompt; restart the server after changing server.py, config.py, telemetry.py or .env. Local runs export traces and logs to Google Cloud like the deployed service; metrics go to Google locally only with cloud.region in OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES (Observability). Set OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=service.namespace=<your-name> in .env so teammates can filter to your traces when reviewing experiments. Full variable reference: Environment Variables.

docs.title: Feature Branch Workflow
docs.text:
# Create branch (feat/, fix/, docs/, refactor/, test/)
git checkout -b feat/your-feature-name

# Develop locally
SERVE_WEB_INTERFACE=TRUE RELOAD_AGENTS=TRUE uv run server

# Commit (Conventional Commits: 50 char title, list body); the hooks run lint/format/typecheck
git add . && git commit -m "feat: add new tool"

# Before pushing: unit tests (100% coverage) and the Postgres integration lane (needs Docker)
# Add --log-cli-level=DEBUG to any run for live logs
uv run pytest --cov
uv run pytest tests/integration

# Push and create PR
git push origin feat/your-feature-name
gh pr create  # Follow PR format: What, Why, How, Tests

# After merge to main, monitor deployment
gh run list --workflow=ci-cd.yml --limit 5
gh run view --log

GitHub Actions automatically builds, tests, and deploys to Cloud Run. Check job summary for deployment details.

docs.title: Code Quality & Testing
docs.text:
The pre-commit hooks lint, format, and type-check every commit. Run the unit tests (100% coverage required) and the integration lane before pushing, and the agent evals when agent behavior changes. The smoke lane needs a deployed service: CI runs it after each deploy, and you can run it against a deployed URL yourself (Smoke Tests).

Standards: - Type Hints: Strict mypy, modern Python syntax (| unions, lowercase generics) - Code Style: Ruff enforced (88-char lines, Path objects, security checks) - Docstrings: Google-style format (args, returns, exceptions) - Testing: 100% coverage on production code, exclusions for configuration modules, fixtures in conftest.py, test behaviors and errors

docs.title: Pre-commit Hooks
docs.text:
Pre-commit runs lint, format, type, and spelling checks as a fix-in-place git hook on every git commit. It does not run pytest. To run the Python tools by hand, the equivalent chain is uv run ruff check --fix && uv run ruff format && uv run mypy, in that order.

CI runs the same hooks with uv run pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure. Run uv run pre-commit run --all-files to check the whole tree the way CI does, like after changing a hook or pulling in upstream changes. In CI, any hook that would modify a file fails the job and prints the diff it would have applied.

Coverage spans Python (ruff, mypy), Terraform (terraform fmt), GitHub Actions workflows (actionlint), the YAML/TOML/JSON config files, and spelling in every text file (codespell). codespell reads [tool.codespell] in pyproject.toml; add a word to ignore-words-list only for a confirmed false positive, with a comment saying why.

Ruff's linter runs before its formatter. ruff check --fix can change layout (removing an else de-indents a block), and the formatter has to see that result. The fix runs only where --fix is passed explicitly; pyproject.toml deliberately does not set fix = true, so a bare ruff check reports instead of rewriting.

terraform validate is deliberately not a hook: it needs terraform init per root, which is too slow for a commit. CI validates instead.

Local tooling: the Terraform hook calls the terraform binary that tenv provides (a prerequisite). tenv reads .terraform-version, the same pin CI installs, so the hook formats exactly as CI does. After the pin changes, run tenv terraform install to fetch the new version. pre-commit builds actionlint itself, using the Go toolchain on PATH if there is one and otherwise downloading one into its own cache. Install shellcheck too: actionlint runs it over workflow run: scripts only when it is on PATH, so without it the hook skips that pass and its findings surface only in CI's code-quality job.

One-time setup (writes .git/hooks/pre-commit):

uv run pre-commit install

Manual invocation:

uv run pre-commit run --all-files              # All hooks on all tracked files
uv run pre-commit run --files path/to/file     # Scope to specific files
uv run pre-commit run ruff-check               # Run a single hook

Hooks are configured in .pre-commit-config.yaml. pre-commit autoupdate is a no-op for the language: system hooks, so update those at their own source:

Hook Version comes from Update with ruff, mypy, codespell uv.lock a Dependabot PR, or uv lock --upgrade terraform fmt .terraform-version, installed by setup-terraform in CI and by tenv locally (tenv provides the terraform on PATH) edit .terraform-version, then tenv terraform install uv-lock your installed uv, held inside required-version (CI uses its pinned setup-uv uv) uv Version everything else the rev in .pre-commit-config.yaml, a commit SHA with a # frozen: vX.Y.Z comment a Dependabot PR, or uv run pre-commit autoupdate --freeze

docs.title: Agent Evals
docs.text:
Run the deterministic agent eval gate before merging changes that touch agent behavior (instructions, tools, callbacks, model):

uv run pytest tests/eval -m "deterministic"     # real model inference, deterministic scoring; needs Vertex creds from .env
uv run pytest tests/eval -m "deterministic" -s  # same, streaming ADK output as each run happens

See Agent Evals for the full evaluation suite reference.

See Testing Strategy and Code Quality references for detailed patterns, tool usage, and exclusion strategies.

docs.title: Connect to Deployed Resources
docs.text:
Run the local agent against the deployed dev session database (Cloud SQL), memory (Agent Engine) and artifact bucket. Docker Compose starts everything this needs: the app container and an IAP tunnel container that reaches Cloud SQL's private IP through the bastion host, so the app connects to localhost:5432 as on Cloud Run.

Important

This path needs a completed deploy and roles/iap.tunnelResourceAccessor on your Google account for the IAP tunnel. Grant it via gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding or the GCP Console.

  1. Open the deploy run's job summary (gh run view <run-id> --web). In the deployed-resource block of .env, uncomment and fill in BASTION_INSTANCE, BASTION_ZONE, SESSION_SERVICE_URI, MEMORY_SERVICE_URI and ARTIFACT_SERVICE_URI, plus any variables you added for your own resources. Set SERVE_WEB_INTERFACE=TRUE in .env too: Compose reads only .env, not your shell. Environment Variables: Cloud Resources says where to find each value.

  2. Start the stack and leave it running:

    docker compose up --build --watch   # Stop: Ctrl+C or docker compose down

    Edits under src/ sync into the container and restart the app; changes to pyproject.toml or uv.lock rebuild the image.

To go back to local storage, comment the service URIs out again and use uv run server. To connect uv run server to individual backends without Compose, see Cloud Backend Options. Watch mode, volumes and the tunnel: Docker Compose Workflow; image layout: Dockerfile Strategy.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
On the schedule in .github/dependabot.yml, Dependabot opens a pull request with minor and patch updates to uv.lock, and a separate one for each major update, which also widens the upper bound in pyproject.toml. Security fixes skip that schedule: Dependabot opens them when an advisory is published, with all open fixes in one pull request. google-adk stays out of both groups, so each ADK bump, version or security, gets its own pull request. Lower bounds stay where they are; to raise one, re-run uv add with the full new constraint, like uv add "pydantic>=2.14.2,<3.0.0" (CI/CD: Action and Hook Pinning). To add or update by hand:

# Add runtime dependency
uv add package-name

# Add dev dependency
uv add --group dev package-name

# Update all dependencies
uv lock --upgrade

# Update specific package
uv lock --upgrade-package package-name

# After updating pyproject.toml or uv.lock:
# - Locally: Restart server or Docker Compose (auto-rebuild with watch)
# - CI/CD: Commit both files together (required for --locked to pass)

docs.title: Version Bump
docs.text:
When bumping version in pyproject.toml:

# Edit version in pyproject.toml
# Then update lockfile
uv lock

# Commit both together
git add pyproject.toml uv.lock
git commit -m "chore: bump version to X.Y.Z"

Why: CI uses uv sync --locked which will fail if lockfile is out of sync.

docs.title: Python Version
docs.text: .python-version names the interpreter. uv reads it locally, and every CI uv python install step runs without a version argument so CI reads it too. Four pins can't read the file and must match it: requires-python, ruff target-version and mypy python_version in pyproject.toml, and both FROM python:<version>-slim stages in the Dockerfile. To move versions, update those pins first (uv python pin rejects a version outside requires-python), run uv python pin X.Y, then uv lock and commit everything together. tests/unit/test_pinned_versions.py fails if any pin drifts, or if a workflow sets its own Python version.

docs.title: uv Version
docs.text:
uv is pinned in two tiers:

  • Your uv: [tool.uv] required-version in pyproject.toml is a range covering one minor series (>=X.Y,<X.(Y+1)). uv refuses every project command, uv run included, when the running uv falls outside it, so any patch of that minor works locally. The uv-lock pre-commit hook runs this uv.
  • CI and the image: the Dockerfile uv image tag and the version: input on every setup-uv step hold one exact version inside that range.

tests/unit/test_pinned_versions.py fails if the exact pins disagree, if a setup-uv step has no version:, or if required-version stops being the exact pin's minor series.

To move uv:

  1. Check the setup-uv release pinned in the workflows: its checksum table (src/download/checksum/known-checksums.json in the action's repo, at that tag) must list the new uv. If it doesn't, move setup-uv to a release that does. Don't pass the action's checksum: input instead: it replaces the per-platform table with one string.
  2. Set the new version in the Dockerfile and every setup-uv version: input.
  3. On a minor bump, move required-version to the new minor series.
  4. Run uv run pytest tests/unit/test_pinned_versions.py, then the full suite.

When your installed uv is outside the range and you don't want to change it, run a pinned uv ad hoc: uvx uv@X.Y.Z <command> uses the pin without touching your install.

docs.title: Custom GCP Services or IAM Roles
docs.text:
Need a new GCP API or WIF IAM role for your feature? Add it to the designated main module extension points — no bootstrap re-run or admin required.

  • terraform/main/services.tf — add to the services set to enable a GCP API
  • terraform/main/iam.tf — add to the wif_additional_roles set to grant the GitHub Actions WIF principal a new role

Add the roles or services AND the resources that use them in the same PR. The time_sleep resources handle propagation within the apply — declare depends_on on the correct sleep instance(s) for any resource that requires a newly-enabled service or role.

See Extending the Main Module for the full pattern, code examples, and rationale.

docs.title: Model Call Timeout
docs.text: ROOT_AGENT_MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS in agent.py caps each model call the agent makes, in evals and in the deployed service. A call that exceeds it raises TimeoutError and is not retried. The limit covers the whole call, including a streamed reply, not just the time to the first token. Size it to your agent's longest legitimate model response, not its whole turn: a long-running workload may also need a longer Cloud Run request timeout, or a background task or queue instead of a synchronous request. The value travels in the agent's generate_content_config (ADK LLM agent configuration) as google-genai's HttpOptions.timeout, in milliseconds; retries are HttpRetryOptions on the same object.

docs.title: Test Deployed Service
docs.text:
Proxy Cloud Run service to test locally:

# Service name format: ${agent_name}-${environment}
gcloud run services proxy <service-name> \
  --project <project-id> \
  --region <region> \
  --port 8000

# Test
curl http://localhost:8000/health

# With web UI (if SERVE_WEB_INTERFACE=TRUE)
open http://localhost:8000

# Stop proxy: Ctrl+C

See Cloud Run proxy documentation.

docs.title: Observability
docs.text:
Server Logs: - Print to stdout (via LoggingPlugin callbacks) - Basic request/response logging for immediate feedback

OpenTelemetry Traces and Logs: - Detailed traces → Cloud Trace - Application logs and GenAI events → Cloud Logging, correlated with traces - ADK metrics → Cloud Monitoring on Cloud Run (locally with cloud.region set)

See Observability for querying, filtering, and trace analysis.

docs.title: Project Structure
docs.text:
your-agent-name/
  src/your_agent_name/
    agent.py              # ADK App and LlmAgent configuration
    callbacks.py          # Agent lifecycle callbacks (logging, safety, tool augmentation)
    prompt.py             # Agent instructions (InstructionProvider pattern)
    config.py             # Typed env-var validation (Pydantic ServerEnv)
    telemetry.py          # OpenTelemetry initialization
    server.py             # FastAPI composition root (services, DI, routing)
    tools.py              # Custom FunctionTools for agent use
  tests/                  # Test suite (unit/integration/smoke/eval lanes)
    unit/conftest.py      # Unit-lane fixtures, mocks, and test env setup
    unit/test_*.py        # Default lane; modules mirror source structure
  terraform/              # Infrastructure as code
    bootstrap/{env}       # One-time CI/CD setup per environment
    main/                 # Agent cloud resource deployment
  docs/                   # Documentation
  .env.example            # Environment template
  pyproject.toml          # Project configuration
  compose.yml             # Local agent against deployed resources
  Dockerfile              # Container image
  AGENTS.md               # AI coding agent instructions (plus tests/, terraform/, .github/workflows/)
  README.md               # Main documentation

Note

Claude Code skips AGENTS.md when a CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md, or CLAUDE.local.md sits in your working directory or above it, and on older versions. See When AGENTS.md support is unavailable for the version floor and the setting that keeps a personal CLAUDE.local.md alongside it.

← Back to Documentation

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Complete configuration reference. Single source of truth.

See .env.example in the repository root for template configuration with inline comments.

Note

A variable set in the environment (your shell, a command prefix like LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG uv run server, or the platform) always wins over the same key in .env. .env only fills in variables that are unset. See Precedence.

docs.title: Quick Reference
docs.text:
Variable Required Default Purpose GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE ✅ - Enable Vertex AI authentication GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT ✅ - GCP project ID GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION ✅ - Vertex AI model endpoint location AGENT_NAME ✅ - Unique agent identifier OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT ✅ - GenAI message content capture mode BASTION_INSTANCE Optional - Bastion host name for IAP tunnel (docker-compose) BASTION_ZONE Optional - Bastion host zone for IAP tunnel (docker-compose) SESSION_SERVICE_URI Optional local SQLite Session persistence MEMORY_SERVICE_URI Optional in-memory Memory persistence ARTIFACT_SERVICE_URI Optional local files Artifact storage LOG_LEVEL Optional INFO Logging verbosity OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES Optional unset Override or add resource attributes OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER Optional unset Replace the template's trace sampler ADK_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT_IN_SPANS Optional true (deployed: false with NO_CONTENT) ADK's live streaming content attribute SERVE_WEB_INTERFACE Optional FALSE Enable ADK web UI RELOAD_AGENTS Optional FALSE Hot-reload on file changes ALLOW_ORIGINS Optional ["http://127.0.0.1:8000", "http://localhost:8000"] CORS allowed origins AGENT_DIR Optional Auto-detected Override agent directory HOST Optional 127.0.0.1 Server bind address PORT Optional 8000 Server listening port ADK_EXPERIMENTAL_TELEMETRY Optional FALSE (template sets TRUE) ADK's experimental metrics and span data ADK_SUPPRESS_EXPERIMENTAL_FEATURE_WARNINGS Optional FALSE Suppress ADK warnings

Cloud Run auto-set: K_CONFIGURATION

CI/CD only: TF_VAR_* variables and repository secrets (GitHub Actions)

Test lanes: test lane inputs (set by CI, or as a prefix on a local test command)

docs.title: Required
docs.text: These must be set for the agent to function.

docs.title: Google Cloud Vertex AI
docs.text:
GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE - Value: TRUE - Purpose: Enables Vertex AI authentication for Gemini models - Where: Set locally in .env, auto-configured in Cloud Run - Note: Replaces GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI, deprecated in ADK 2.4.0. The old name still resolves, but every request that reads it emits a DeprecationWarning. Update an existing local .env to silence it. When both are set, GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE wins

GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT - Value: Your GCP project ID (e.g., your-project-id) - Purpose: Identifies the Google Cloud project for Vertex AI and other GCP services - Where: Set locally in .env, configured via Terraform for Cloud Run

GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION - Value: Vertex AI model endpoint location (e.g., global or us-central1) - Purpose: Routes Vertex AI model calls only. Does not set the deployment region. Infrastructure placement is controlled separately by the region Terraform variable (REGION GitHub Environment Variable) - Where: Set locally in .env, configured via Terraform for Cloud Run (TF_VAR_google_cloud_location)

docs.title: Agent Identification
docs.text: AGENT_NAME - Value: Unique identifier (e.g., your-agent) - Purpose: Identifies cloud resources, logs, and traces - Where: Set locally in .env, set before bootstrap (used for Terraform resource naming) - Note: Used as base name for Terraform resources ({agent_name}-{environment})

docs.title: OpenTelemetry
docs.text:
OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT - Options (exact, uppercase; ServerEnv rejects anything else, including TRUE and FALSE): - NO_CONTENT - No message content (pair with ADK_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT_IN_SPANS=false to keep live streaming content out too) - EVENT_ONLY - Put prompts and responses on gen_ai.client.inference.operation.details log records (GenAI events), shown in Cloud Trace's Input/Output view - SPAN_ONLY - Put them on span attributes: gen_ai.input.messages and gen_ai.output.messages on model calls, gen_ai.tool.call.arguments and gen_ai.tool.call.result on tool calls - SPAN_AND_EVENT - Both - Purpose: Controls whether and where ADK records GenAI message content, including tool arguments and results. Live streaming content follows ADK_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT_IN_SPANS instead - Where: Set locally in .env, set before bootstrap - Reference: Message Content Capture (recommended values and why) and OpenTelemetry's GenAI utilities - Security: For sensitive data, set NO_CONTENT and ADK_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT_IN_SPANS=false

ADK_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT_IN_SPANS - Default: true when unset (ADK's default, independent of the capture mode); the Cloud Run service sets false whenever its capture mode is NO_CONTENT - Purpose: Read by ADK, not ServerEnv. Under ADK's default telemetry schema it only controls live streaming (/run_live): the content sent to the model, on the gcp.vertex.agent.data span attribute. It also controls content on ADK's deprecated legacy schema (ADK_TELEMETRY_SCHEMA_VERSION_OPT_IN=otel_semconv_1_36). false leaves them empty - Where: .env locally; derived from the capture mode in terraform/main/main.tf on Cloud Run - Reference: Message Content Capture

docs.title: Cloud Resources
docs.text:
Deployed persistence for sessions, memory, and artifacts. Set locally to run against deployed resources: all of them for Docker Compose (Development: Connect to Deployed Resources), or individual URIs for uv run server (Cloud Backend Options). uv run server and Compose read the same .env. Terraform sets the service URIs on Cloud Run; the bastion values are local only. Unset, ADK stores sessions and artifacts locally under src/<package>/.adk/ and keeps memory in-process.

BASTION_INSTANCE - Value: Bastion VM instance name (e.g., my-agent-dev-bastion) - Purpose: IAP tunnel target for docker-compose Cloud SQL connectivity - Where: Set locally in .env for docker-compose (the IAP tunnel container uses this) - How to get: GitHub Actions job summary or terraform output bastion_instance - Note: Only used by docker-compose, not by the application. Cloud Run connects to Cloud SQL via direct VPC egress.

BASTION_ZONE - Value: GCE zone (e.g., us-central1-b) - Purpose: Zone of the bastion host for IAP tunnel - Where: Set locally in .env for docker-compose - How to get: GitHub Actions job summary or terraform output bastion_zone - Note: Only used by docker-compose.

SESSION_SERVICE_URI - Value: Service-specific URI with protocol prefix (e.g., postgresql+asyncpg://sa-name@project.iam:@localhost:5432/agent_sessions) - Purpose: Session persistence (production-consistent behavior) - Where: Set locally in .env for Docker Compose, auto-configured in Cloud Run - How to get: GitHub Actions job summary (gh run view <run-id>) or terraform output session_service_uri - Note: Database Session Service connects through Cloud SQL Auth Proxy on localhost. IAM database auth — no password needed. Unset: SQLite under src/<package>/.adk/, kept across restarts.

MEMORY_SERVICE_URI - Value: Service-specific URI with protocol prefix (e.g., agentengine://projects/123/locations/us-central1/reasoningEngines/456) - Purpose: Memory persistence (production-consistent behavior) - Where: Set locally in .env for Docker Compose, auto-configured in Cloud Run - How to get: GitHub Actions job summary (gh run view <run-id>) or terraform output memory_service_uri - Note: Unset: in-memory, reset on restart

ARTIFACT_SERVICE_URI - Value: GCS bucket URI (e.g., gs://your-artifact-bucket) - Purpose: Artifact storage persistence (production-consistent behavior) - Where: Set locally in .env for Docker Compose, auto-configured in Cloud Run - How to get: GitHub Actions job summary (gh run view <run-id>) or GCP Console (Cloud Storage → Buckets) - Note: Unset: files under src/<package>/.adk/artifacts/

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
LOG_LEVEL - Options: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL - Default: INFO - Purpose: Controls logging verbosity - Where: Set locally via .env or command line, configure via GitHub Environment Variables for Cloud Run - Usage: 

LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG uv run server

docs.title: OpenTelemetry Export
docs.text:
Every signal exports to the Google Cloud Telemetry API with Application Default Credentials. telemetry.py passes the endpoint to every exporter explicitly, so the SDK's OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_* endpoint variables have no effect. On Cloud Run, metrics go to Google automatically; locally they go only when you add cloud.region=<region> to OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES. The OpenTelemetry SDK reads these variables itself, from .env or the shell.

Note

Only uv run server and the container entry point run the template's telemetry setup. adk web, adk api_server and adk run use ADK's own telemetry setup instead.

OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES - Default: unset (no service.namespace) - Purpose: Override or add resource attributes on every signal. A key set here wins over the template's value (like service.name). Set service.namespace to a unique value, like your name, so teammates can filter to your local experiments - Where: .env or the shell; Terraform sets service.namespace=<environment> on the Cloud Run service - Format: comma-separated key=value pairs, like OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=service.name=my-agent,service.namespace=alice-local - Metrics locally: add cloud.region=<region> (like cloud.region=us-central1) to send metrics to Google from your machine; without a region, metrics are off - Note: The SDK also honors the standard OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, which wins over service.name in OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES; the template neither sets nor prints it

OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER - Default: unset (the template's sampler records every span, including under Cloud Run's unsampled traceparent) - Purpose: Replace the template's trace sampler with a standard SDK one, read with OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG. Pick one that ignores the parent's sampled flag, like traceidratio: a parent-based sampler drops most agent spans on Cloud Run. Why: OpenTelemetry Architecture - Where: .env or the shell; not set on the Cloud Run service

The SDK reads its other standard variables too; the template sets none of them on Cloud Run. See the OpenTelemetry SDK environment variables.

docs.title: Agent Features
docs.text:
SERVE_WEB_INTERFACE - Default: FALSE - Purpose: Enables ADK web UI at http://127.0.0.1:8000 - Where: Set locally via .env, configure via GitHub Environment Variables for Cloud Run - Options: - FALSE - API-only mode - TRUE - Enable web interface

RELOAD_AGENTS - Default: FALSE - Purpose: Enable agent hot-reloading on file changes (development only) - Where: Local development only - WARNING: Set to FALSE in production (Cloud Run forces FALSE)

docs.title: CORS
docs.text: ALLOW_ORIGINS - Default: '["http://127.0.0.1:8000", "http://localhost:8000"]' - Format: JSON array string - Purpose: Configure CORS allowed origins - Where: Hard-coded in Terraform for Cloud Run, configurable locally via .env - Example: ALLOW_ORIGINS='["https://your-domain.com", "http://127.0.0.1:3000"]'

docs.title: Advanced
docs.text:
AGENT_DIR - Default: Auto-detected (the directory containing the agent package relative to server.py) - Purpose: Override agent directory path for ADK - Where: Rarely needed; the default resolves to src/ locally and /app/src in the container - Note: Only override if you need non-standard directory structure

HOST - Default: 127.0.0.1 - Purpose: Server bind address - Where: Rarely needs override - defaults work for most use cases - Note: The Dockerfile sets 0.0.0.0 so the container accepts connections from outside itself

PORT - Default: 8000 - Purpose: Server listening port - Where: Rarely needs override - Cloud Run always uses 8000, Docker Compose maps to host port 8000 - Note: Only override if you have port conflicts on your local machine

ADK_EXPERIMENTAL_TELEMETRY - Default: FALSE when unset; .env.example and the Cloud Run service (terraform/main/main.tf) set TRUE - Purpose: Read by ADK, not ServerEnv. Adds ADK's adk.experimental.* metrics (token breakdowns, workflow call counts, skill loads, compactions) and experimental span data. ADK's seven default gen_ai.* metrics need no flag - Where: .env locally; fixed in the Terraform env map on Cloud Run

ADK_SUPPRESS_EXPERIMENTAL_FEATURE_WARNINGS - Default: FALSE - Purpose: Suppress ADK experimental feature warnings - Options: - FALSE - Show warnings - TRUE - Suppress warnings

docs.title: Cloud Run Auto-Set (Read-Only)
docs.text:
These variables are automatically set by Cloud Run. Do not set manually.

K_CONFIGURATION - Default: unset (local development) - Purpose: Cloud Run configuration name. telemetry.py reads it for the configuration_name label that places OTLP logs on the cloud_run_revision resource; the GCP resource detector supplies the other labels - Where: Auto-set by Cloud Run - Example: your-agent-dev

docs.title: CI/CD Only
docs.text: These variables are used exclusively in GitHub Actions workflows. Do not set locally.

docs.title: Terraform Inputs (TF_VAR_*)
docs.text:
GitHub Environment Variables are mapped to Terraform inputs via TF_VAR_* prefix:

TF_VAR_project - Source: ${{ vars.GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT }} (GitHub Environment Variable) - Purpose: GCP project ID for Terraform

TF_VAR_region - Source: ${{ vars.REGION }} (GitHub Environment Variable) - Purpose: GCP region for compute resource placement

TF_VAR_zone - Source: ${{ vars.ZONE }} (GitHub Environment Variable) - Purpose: GCP zone for bastion host placement

TF_VAR_google_cloud_location - Source: ${{ vars.GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION }} (GitHub Environment Variable, optional) - Purpose: Vertex AI model endpoint routing (recommended default "global" in bootstrap terraform.tfvars.example)

TF_VAR_agent_name - Source: ${{ vars.IMAGE_NAME }} (GitHub Environment Variable) - Purpose: Agent name for resource naming

TF_VAR_terraform_state_bucket - Source: ${{ vars.TERRAFORM_STATE_BUCKET }} (GitHub Environment Variable) - Purpose: GCS bucket for Terraform state

TF_VAR_otel_instrumentation_genai_capture_message_content - Source: ${{ vars.OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT }} (GitHub Environment Variable, written by bootstrap from otel_instrumentation_genai_capture_message_content in each bootstrap root's terraform.tfvars) - Purpose: Message content capture mode on the Cloud Run service. Required: Terraform validation accepts only the four capture modes, so deleting the GitHub variable fails the plan. With NO_CONTENT, Terraform also sets ADK_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT_IN_SPANS=false - Recommended: SPAN_AND_EVENT in dev to debug prompts, responses and tool calls; NO_CONTENT in stage and prod (the bootstrap terraform.tfvars.example files) - Change: set the bootstrap value and re-apply bootstrap, which rewrites the GitHub variable

TF_VAR_docker_image - Source: ${{ inputs.docker_image }} (workflow input) - Purpose: Immutable image digest for deployment

TF_VAR_environment - Source: Set by workflow (dev/stage/prod) - Purpose: Environment-specific resource naming

TF_VAR_workload_identity_pool_principal_identifier - Source: ${{ vars.WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_POOL_PRINCIPAL_IDENTIFIER }} (GitHub Environment Variable, auto-created by bootstrap) - Purpose: WIF principal identifier for binding additional IAM roles in terraform/main/iam.tf

docs.title: Runtime Configuration Overrides
docs.text:
Override runtime config via GitHub Environment Variables (mapped to TF_VAR_*):

TF_VAR_log_level - Source: ${{ vars.LOG_LEVEL }} (optional GitHub Environment Variable) - Purpose: Override LOG_LEVEL for Cloud Run deployment

TF_VAR_serve_web_interface - Source: ${{ vars.SERVE_WEB_INTERFACE }} (optional GitHub Environment Variable) - Purpose: Override SERVE_WEB_INTERFACE for Cloud Run deployment - Set: gh variable set SERVE_WEB_INTERFACE --env dev --body "TRUE" (or Settings → Environments), then re-run the latest CI/CD workflow to redeploy. The web interface is then at http://localhost:8000 through gcloud run services proxy

docs.title: Test Lane Inputs
docs.text:
Read by test lanes rather than by the application, so they never appear in ServerEnv or on Cloud Run. CI sets them from workflow inputs; set them locally only to run a lane by hand, as a prefix on the command itself.

Note

.env does not set these. The smoke lane never loads .env at all and raises on an unset SMOKE_*. The eval lane takes no environment input: what it scores is fixed in constants in tests/eval/test_agent_eval.py, so a run cannot be reconfigured from outside the file it is defined in.

SMOKE_BASE_URL, SMOKE_INVOKER_SA - Source: smoke.yml, from the apply job's smoke_target_url and smoke_invoker_service_account_email outputs - Purpose: Deployed service URL and the invoker SA the smoke client impersonates. See Smoke Tests

INTEGRATION_DATABASE_URI - Source: Not set in CI (the lane starts a throwaway postgres:18 via testcontainers) - Purpose: Point the integration lane at an already-running Postgres instead. See Integration Tests

docs.title: Repository Secrets
docs.text:
Set in GitHub Actions > Secrets and variables > Actions. Both select the model auth path for the claude.yml PR review; when neither is set, the review authenticates via Workload Identity Federation and calls Vertex AI. See Claude PR Review.

ANTHROPIC_API_KEY - Source: Repository secret (optional, set manually) - Purpose: Runs the review against the Anthropic API with an organization API key instead of Vertex AI. Takes precedence over CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN

CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN - Source: Repository secret (optional, set manually; generate with claude setup-token) - Purpose: Runs the review against the Anthropic API with an individual account's Claude Code OAuth token instead of Vertex AI. Ignored when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set. Expires about a year after creation and must be rotated

Note

These two names are also what the local Claude Code CLI reads for its own authentication. The "do not set locally" guidance above applies to the TF_VAR_* variables, not to these.

docs.title: Where Variables Are Set
docs.text:
Local Development: - .env file in the directory where you run the server - Command line (e.g., LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG uv run server) - compose.yml (Docker Compose)

Cloud Run: - Terraform main module (terraform/main/main.tf) - GitHub Environment Variables → TF_VAR_* → Terraform → Cloud Run environment

CI/CD: - GitHub Environment Variables (auto-created by bootstrap) - Workflow inputs and outputs

docs.title: Precedence
docs.text:
The environment wins over .env, everywhere .env is read:

  1. initialize_environment() (config.py) runs first in server.py. It finds .env by searching upward from the working directory and copies it into os.environ with python-dotenv's load_dotenv(), without overriding any variable already set. ServerEnv then reads os.environ; .env keys it does not define are ignored.
  2. ADK's agent loader then finds .env by searching upward from the agent's package and loads it with override=True, but first snapshots every variable already in os.environ and restores those after loading. Everything initialize_environment() set is in that snapshot, so ADK only adds keys that neither the environment nor the working directory's .env set. adk web, adk api_server and adk run skip step 1, so there ADK's loader is the only one.
  3. The eval lane loads .env with python-dotenv without overriding set variables.

Because .env reaches os.environ before anything else in startup, every reader sees it: ServerEnv, the OpenTelemetry SDK's OTEL_* variables, ADK, and the Google SDKs.

Cloud Run never reads .env (.dockerignore keeps it out of the image), and Docker Compose passes it to the container through env_file:, so the platform's values always apply there.

Note

A variable exported in your shell profile, like a global GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT, overrides this project's .env. Unset it or run the server from a shell without it when the two differ.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Never commit .env files to version control - Already gitignored
  • Workload Identity Federation - No service account keys needed for CI/CD
  • Sensitive data - Set OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT=NO_CONTENT and ADK_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT_IN_SPANS=false when handling sensitive information

← Back to Documentation

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
First-time setup: from a fresh repository to an agent running locally, then deployed.

Note

Bootstrap is a one-time setup per GitHub Environment. After the first deployment, use the feature branch workflow described in Development.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Required: - tenv to install Terraform at the version pinned in .terraform-version (run tenv terraform install from the repo root) - Google Cloud SDK (gcloud CLI) - GitHub CLI (gh) - uv, within the required-version range in pyproject.toml (it installs the Python version in .python-version) - jq command-line JSON processor (for parsing Terraform output)

Warning

Install Terraform through tenv, not on its own. CI installs exactly the version in .terraform-version, and a standalone terraform ignores that file, so your local version drifts from CI's and terraform fmt and plans can differ from what CI produces.

GCP Project: - Create a new GCP project (or use existing) - Enable billing - Owner role

GitHub Repository: - Create a new repository from this template - Admin access (for GitHub Environments and Variables)

docs.title: 1. Authenticate
docs.text:
Choose your dev project ID now. Use the same ID for GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT in .env below, and for projects.dev in pre-bootstrap and project in the dev bootstrap configuration later.

gcloud auth login
gcloud config set project YOUR_DEV_PROJECT_ID
gcloud auth application-default login
gcloud auth application-default set-quota-project YOUR_DEV_PROJECT_ID
gh auth login

ADC login can set the quota project automatically; the explicit command confirms the intended project. For quota and billing errors, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: 2. Enable the APIs for a Local Run
docs.text:
The local agent calls Gemini through Vertex AI and exports traces and logs through the Telemetry API.

gcloud services enable aiplatform.googleapis.com telemetry.googleapis.com

docs.title: 3. Install and Test
docs.text:
uv sync                      # Create .venv with runtime and dev dependencies
uv run pre-commit install    # Run the CI quality checks on each commit
uv run pytest --cov          # Unit tests, 100% coverage required

docs.title: 4. Configure .env
docs.text:
cp .env.example .env

Set GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT to your dev project ID. Leave the deployed-resource block commented out: with those URIs unset, the agent stores sessions and artifacts locally.

docs.title: Run the Agent Locally
docs.text:
SERVE_WEB_INTERFACE=TRUE uv run server

The web interface is at http://localhost:8000. Sessions persist in SQLite under src/<package>/.adk/ (gitignored), so you can stop the server and return to a previous conversation, like with adk web. Memory is in-process only and resets on restart.

Tip

Add RELOAD_AGENTS=TRUE to reload the agent, tools, callbacks and prompt when you edit them, with no restart. Changes to server.py, config.py, telemetry.py or .env still require a restart.

Local options and connecting to deployed resources: Development.

docs.title: Bootstrap CI/CD
docs.text: Bootstrap creates the one-time CI/CD infrastructure for the dev environment: keyless GitHub Actions authentication, the image registry, and the GitHub Environment and its variables. Bootstrap Reference lists every resource and covers production mode.

docs.title: 1. Create State Buckets (Pre-Bootstrap)
docs.text:
Pre-bootstrap creates the GCS state buckets used by bootstrap and the main module.

cp terraform/bootstrap/pre/terraform.tfvars.example terraform/bootstrap/pre/terraform.tfvars
# Edit terraform.tfvars: set agent_name and GCP project IDs

terraform -chdir=terraform/bootstrap/pre init
terraform -chdir=terraform/bootstrap/pre apply

See Bootstrap Reference: Pre-Bootstrap for scope options (dev-only, full production, incremental) and how to skip pre-bootstrap if you already have a GCS bucket.

docs.title: 2. Configure
docs.text:
Dev-only mode (default): bootstrap only the dev environment.

cp terraform/bootstrap/dev/terraform.tfvars.example terraform/bootstrap/dev/terraform.tfvars

Fill in every value under the REQUIRED header in terraform.tfvars; the comments in the file describe each one. agent_name must match pre-bootstrap, and terraform_state_bucket comes from the pre-bootstrap terraform_state_buckets output.

Note

For production mode (dev → stage → prod), see Infrastructure.

docs.title: 3. Bootstrap
docs.text:
terraform -chdir=terraform/bootstrap/dev init \
  -backend-config="bucket=$(terraform -chdir=terraform/bootstrap/pre output -json terraform_state_buckets | jq -r '.dev')"
terraform -chdir=terraform/bootstrap/dev apply

Confirm the GitHub Environment variables exist:

gh variable list --env dev  # or GitHub repo Settings > Environments > dev

docs.title: 4. Set Up Claude PR Review
docs.text: Opening a pull request triggers an automated Claude code review. It needs a one-time setup before the first PR: install the Claude GitHub App, then pick a model auth path, either Vertex AI in the dev project or a direct Anthropic credential. See Claude PR Review.

docs.title: Deploy
docs.text: Merging to main deploys the agent's infrastructure and Cloud Run service to dev. Infrastructure: Terraform Structure lists what the main module creates.

docs.title: 1. Create Pull Request
docs.text:
git checkout -b feat/initial-setup
git add .
git commit -m "feat: initial setup"
git push origin feat/initial-setup
gh pr create --title "feat: initial setup" --body "Initial agent deployment"

docs.title: 2. Review and Merge
docs.text:
1. Review the Terraform plan in the PR comments
  2. Merge the PR (triggers deployment to dev)

docs.title: 3. Monitor Deployment
docs.text:
gh run list --workflow=ci-cd.yml --limit 5
gh run view <run-id> --web   # Job summary: Cloud Run URL and resource URIs
gh run view <run-id> --log   # Full logs

The job summary lists the deployed resource values. You need them only to run a local agent against deployed resources (Development: Connect to Deployed Resources).

docs.title: Run the Deployed Agent
docs.text:
Proxy the deployed Cloud Run service to your machine:

# Service name format: ${AGENT_NAME}-${environment} (like your-agent-dev)
gcloud run services proxy <service-name> --project <project-id> --region <region> --port 8000

# In another terminal
curl http://localhost:8000/health  # Expected: {"status": "ok"}

The deployed service serves the web interface only when enabled; see TF_VAR_serve_web_interface in Environment Variables.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Development: feature branch workflow, testing, and code quality
  • Infrastructure: deployment modes, pipeline behavior, and operations
  • Release a Version: one-time GitHub App setup, then release pull requests and production promotion
  • Observability: traces and logs in Cloud Trace and Cloud Logging, with query examples

← Back to Documentation

docs.title: Infrastructure
docs.text:
Deployment, CI/CD, and infrastructure management.

Important

Complete bootstrap setup and configure protection rules before deploying in Production Mode.

docs.title: Bootstrap Setup
docs.text:
Bootstrap creates CI/CD infrastructure one time per environment: - Workload Identity Federation (keyless GitHub Actions auth) - Artifact Registry (Docker images with cleanup policies) - Terraform State Bucket (remote state for main module) - GitHub Environments and Variables - Tag protection and cross-project IAM (production mode)

First time? See Getting Started for complete walkthrough including prerequisites.

Setting up production mode or need full detail? See Bootstrap Reference.

docs.title: Protection Strategies
docs.text:
Configure protection rules after bootstrap (manual setup):

Branch Protection (main): 1. Settings → Branches → Add rule for main 2. Require PR with 1 approval, dismiss stale reviews 3. Require status checks: CI / status 4. No force pushes, no deletions

Tag Protection (production mode, automated): - Bootstrap creates a ruleset that lets only repository admins create prod-v* promotion tags - Verify: Settings → Rules → Rulesets

Environment Protection (production mode, automated): - Set the prod_apply_* variables in terraform/bootstrap/prod/terraform.tfvars (reviewers, self-review, admin bypass, wait timer), then apply the prod bootstrap root - Bootstrap also limits the prod and prod-apply environments to prod-v*.*.* tags, and stage to main plus those tags. Each environment's WIF provider accepts only tokens from those environments, so no other ref can authenticate to stage or prod (except on private GitHub Free repositories, which lack deployment policies: Protection Strategies)

See Protection Strategies for the settings, verification and rationale.

docs.title: Deployment Modes
docs.text:
Dev-Only Mode: - Single GCP project, single environment - Workflow: PR → plan, Merge → deploy to dev - Use: Experiments, prototypes, internal tools

Production Mode: - Three GCP projects (dev/stage/prod) - Workflow: PR → plan, Merge → dev+stage, prod-vX.Y.Z promotion tag → prod (approval required) - Release steps: Release a Version - Use: Production services, staged deployment, compliance

Switch modes: Edit production_mode in .github/workflows/ci-cd.yml

See Deployment Modes for mode comparison, workflow details, and switching instructions.

docs.title: Workflow Behavior
docs.text:
What GitHub Actions does at each trigger:

PR Flow: - Builds Docker image → pushes to dev registry as pr-{number}-{sha} - Runs Terraform plan for dev - Comments plan on PR - No deployment

Merge Flow (dev-only mode): - Builds image → pushes as {sha}, latest - Deploys to dev

Merge Flow (production mode): - Builds image → pushes to dev registry - Deploys to dev and stage (parallel after build)

Tag Flow (production mode): - Resolves image from stage registry - Promotes to prod registry - Deploys to prod (requires approval in prod-apply environment)

See CI/CD Workflows for workflow architecture, job details, and customization.

docs.title: Deploy to Dev (Automatic)
docs.text:
Create PR and merge to main: 

# Create feature branch
git checkout -b feat/your-feature

# Make changes, commit
git add .
git commit -m "feat: add new feature"

# Push and create PR
git push origin feat/your-feature
gh pr create

# After approval, merge PR (via GitHub UI or CLI)
gh pr merge --squash

GitHub Actions automatically builds and deploys to dev (+ stage in production mode) when PR is merged.

Monitor: Actions tab → CI/CD Pipeline

docs.title: Enable Dev Deployment on Pull Request (Optional)
docs.text:
Note

By default, the pipeline deploys to dev only on merge to main. Enable PR deploys to deploy dev on every PR for immediate feedback in live environment.

Impact: - Every PR and commit deploys to dev (concurrency prevents simultaneous deploys: new commits cancel in-progress PR deploys) - Dev becomes unstable (last PR wins) - Requires team coordination for concurrent PRs - Useful for complex integrations requiring live environment testing

Enable: Change the dev-apply job's condition in .github/workflows/ci-cd.yml: 

# From:
if: github.ref_type == 'branch' && github.event_name == 'push'

# To:
if: github.ref_type == 'branch'

docs.title: Release and Promote to Production
docs.text: Releases, production promotion, hotfixes and rollback: Release a Version.

docs.title: View Workflow Status
docs.text:
GitHub Actions UI: 1. Actions tab → CI/CD Pipeline 2. Click run to view: - Job summaries (deployment outputs, Cloud Run URL, resources) - Individual job logs - PR plan comments

GitHub CLI: 

# List recent runs
gh run list --workflow=ci-cd.yml --limit 5

# View specific run
gh run view <run-id>

# View logs
gh run view <run-id> --log

docs.title: Trace Deployed Image
docs.text:
# Get deployed image
IMAGE=$(gcloud run services describe <service> \
  --region <region> \
  --format='value(spec.template.spec.containers[0].image)')

# Get commit SHA (first tag)
gcloud artifacts docker images describe "$IMAGE" \
  --format="value(tags)" | cut -d',' -f1

docs.title: View Traces and Logs
docs.text:
Cloud Console: - Cloud Trace → Trace Explorer - Logs Explorer

See Observability for query examples and trace analysis.

docs.title: Terraform Structure
docs.text:
Bootstrap Module (terraform/bootstrap/{dev,stage,prod}/): - One-time CI/CD infrastructure per environment (WIF, Artifact Registry, GitHub environments/variables) - Remote state in GCS (buckets created by pre-bootstrap, which keeps local state), runs manually by infrastructure owners

Main Module (terraform/main/): - VPC networking: VPC + subnet + Private Services Access, Cloud NAT, IAP firewall rules - Bastion host: e2-micro (COS), Auth Proxy via cloud-init, dedicated SA that impersonates app SA (--impersonate-service-account) for IAM database auth - Application deployment: Cloud Run (Auth Proxy sidecar + direct VPC egress), app SA, Cloud SQL Postgres (private IP), Agent Engine, GCS bucket - Remote state (bucket created by bootstrap), runs automatically in CI/CD - Extend with custom GCP APIs (services.tf) and WIF IAM roles (iam.tf) via Pull Requests — see Extending the Main Module

See Deployment Modes: Terraform Structure for resource details and naming conventions.

docs.title: Upgrading Provider Lockfiles
docs.text:
Dependabot keeps providers current through two terraform entries in .github/dependabot.yml, both with the same cooldown as actions and hooks. Constraints allow any release below the next major, so minor and patch releases need no constraint edit.

  • terraform/main: one pull request with every provider update. Its Plan Dev shows what the new version changes, and merging applies it to dev, so confirm the plan before you merge.
  • Bootstrap roots and modules: one pull request per provider across all of them. CI never runs bootstrap, so after merging, run terraform init and terraform plan in each bootstrap root, confirm the plan, and apply if it shows changes.

Tip

If you don't plan to re-run bootstrap after the initial setup, delete the bootstrap entry from .github/dependabot.yml to stop those pull requests. Upgrade the bootstrap lockfiles by hand before you next run it.

To bump by hand, regenerate the lockfiles:

Main module (terraform/main/) runs in CI/CD on linux_amd64, so its lockfile needs both local and CI platform hashes:

cd terraform/main
terraform init -upgrade -backend=false
terraform providers lock -platform=darwin_arm64 -platform=linux_amd64

Bootstrap modules (terraform/bootstrap/) only run locally, so a single-platform init is sufficient:

cd terraform/bootstrap/dev
terraform init -upgrade -backend=false
# Copy updated lockfile to stage and prod (same providers, same versions)
cp .terraform.lock.hcl ../stage/.terraform.lock.hcl
cp .terraform.lock.hcl ../prod/.terraform.lock.hcl

Note

terraform/bootstrap/pre/ uses different providers (random instead of github) — upgrade it separately with terraform init -upgrade -backend=false.

docs.title: Cloud SQL Scaling
docs.text:
The template ships with db-custom-1-3840 (1 vCPU, 3.75 GB RAM) — should handle ~100 concurrent database connections. Each Cloud Run instance maintains a connection pool (default 5 + 10 overflow = 15 max), so this supports ~6 concurrent instances comfortably.

Scaling path:

  1. Bump instance tier — change tier in database.tf (e.g., db-custom-2-7680 for ~200 connections). One-line change, applies via in-place restart (~5 minutes).
  2. Managed connection pooling — if autoscaling demands exceed tier capacity, enable Cloud SQL connection pooling (requires Enterprise Plus edition). No app code changes — Auth Proxy handles routing automatically.

See the Cloud SQL planning guide for tiers, editions, storage, availability, and cache options.

docs.title: Image Promotion (Production Mode)
docs.text:
Production mode promotes images between registries instead of rebuilding, ensuring exact tested bytes deploy across environments:

Dev → Stage: Triggered on merge to main Stage → Prod: Triggered on a prod-vX.Y.Z promotion tag push (requires manual approval)

Cross-project IAM for promotion is configured automatically during bootstrap.

See Deployment Modes: Image Promotion for promotion details and cross-project IAM.

← Back to Documentation

docs.title: Agent Observability with OpenTelemetry
docs.text: The server exports traces, logs and metrics over OTLP gRPC to Google Cloud, with the same setup locally and on Cloud Run. The ADK web UI keeps its trace view when enabled.

docs.title: What's Instrumented
docs.text:
• Agent runs: ADK spans for each invocation, agent, model call and tool call, plus ADK's GenAI metrics (operation duration, token usage, agent and tool call counts, and the adk.experimental.* breakdowns that ADK_EXPERIMENTAL_TELEMETRY adds) whenever metrics are on
  • GenAI events: Model call details as log records, with message content when capture is on
  • Application logs: Python logging records with trace context, including the callback logging

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Owned providers: configure_telemetry() sets the tracer, logger and (when the resource has cloud.region) meter providers before get_fast_api_app(); ADK only attaches its web UI processors to them
  • Google Cloud: Traces and logs go to the Telemetry API with Application Default Credentials, landing in Cloud Trace and Cloud Logging
  • Metrics where a location is known: On Cloud Run, metrics go to Google automatically. Locally they go to Google only when you add cloud.region=<region> to OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES; otherwise they are off. Google metrics land in Cloud Monitoring beside Cloud Run's native metrics
  • One backend: Telemetry targets Google Cloud only. To use another backend, replace telemetry.py
  • Consistent resource: Every signal carries the same identifying attributes: service.name from AGENT_NAME, service.namespace per environment, a unique service.instance.id per process, and the Cloud Run revision as faas.version from the resource detector
  • Cloud Run logs in place: On Cloud Run, the traces and logs resource adds the cloud_run_revision attributes, so logs appear in the service's Logs tab beside stdout. Metrics use a separate resource without them, because the Telemetry API drops metric points that carry gcp.resource_type, so metric queries cannot filter on revision labels

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Required environment variables: - AGENT_NAME: OpenTelemetry service.name (required) - GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT: GCP project ID (required) - OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT: Message content capture mode (required, see Message Content Capture)

Optional variables: - LOG_LEVEL: Logging verbosity - DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL (default: INFO) - OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES: override or add resource attributes, like OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=service.namespace=alice-local to group your local experiments (Terraform sets service.namespace to the environment name when deployed)

Details and defaults: Environment Variables.

Note

Only uv run server and the container entry point run this setup. adk web, adk api_server and adk run use ADK's own telemetry setup instead.

docs.title: Viewing Telemetry in Google Cloud
docs.text:
Cloud Trace: Filter by service name, view spans, timing, and generative AI events. Every agent request is traced. On Cloud Run, the agent spans continue the trace Cloud Run starts for the request, so a request log entry's trace link, the application logs and the agent spans share one trace ID. Sampling and how to override it: OpenTelemetry Architecture.

On Cloud Run, an agent trace usually has no stored root span: Cloud Run stores its own span only for requests it samples, at most 0.1 per second per instance, so the invoke_workflow span points at a missing parent. Find agent turns by span name invoke_workflow, not with root-span filters.

On Cloud Run, a request's traces, logs and metrics can arrive late on a quiet service, because CPU is allocated only during requests. Causes and options: OpenTelemetry Architecture.

Logs Explorer: Application logs land in the log otlp and GenAI events in gen_ai.client.inference.operation.details. On Cloud Run both are on the cloud_run_revision resource; locally they are on generic_task.

logName="projects/{PROJECT_ID}/logs/otlp"
resource.type="cloud_run_revision"
resource.labels.service_name="{AGENT_NAME}-{ENVIRONMENT}"

Metrics Explorer: ADK's GenAI metrics (like gen_ai.client.token.usage) appear as prometheus.googleapis.com/<name>/<kind> on the prometheus_target resource, beside Cloud Run's native metrics on the service's Metrics tab. On Cloud Run, metrics go to Google automatically. Locally they go to Google only when you add cloud.region=<region> to OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES; otherwise they are off.

docs.title: gcloud CLI
docs.text:
# Tail the service's OpenTelemetry logs
gcloud logging tail 'logName="projects/{PROJECT_ID}/logs/otlp" AND resource.type="cloud_run_revision"' --format=json

# View recent traces
gcloud trace list --limit=10

docs.title: VS Code GCP Extension
docs.text: Install the Google Cloud Code extension to view logs and traces directly in your IDE.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
server.py calls configure_telemetry() before get_fast_api_app(). It builds the resource and the tracer, logger and meter providers (the meter provider only when the resource has cloud.region), sets them globally, and instruments logging. telemetry.py replaces ADK's internal telemetry setup with a function that only attaches the web UI's span and log processors to those providers, so ADK builds no providers, exporters or instrumentation of its own.

Design decisions, the ADK patch, and dependencies: OpenTelemetry Architecture.

docs.title: Resource Attributes
docs.text:
Attribute Source Example service.name AGENT_NAME your-agent-name service.namespace OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES (unset by default) dev/stage/prod (deployed) or alice-local service.instance.id Generated per process (PID + UUID) worker-1234-a1b2c3d4e5f6 gcp.project_id GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT my-project-id cloud.*, faas.* GCP resource detector cloud.region=us-central1, faas.version=your-agent-name-dev-00042-abc on Cloud Run

OTEL_SERVICE_NAME and OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES win over these on a shared key, and the template's values win over the detector's. The standard OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true turns all export off (SDK behavior) and leaves the web UI trace view empty.

docs.title: Alerting
docs.text:
The main module ships dry-run Cloud Monitoring alert policies for the four golden signals (latency, traffic, errors, saturation), plus unhealthy instances, on the deployed Cloud Run service. Each condition reads a native run.googleapis.com metric with the aggregation its chart uses, so every alert maps to a chart on the service's Metrics tab in the Cloud Run console. The template adds alert policies only, no dashboard.

Policy Metric Default condition Metrics tab chart Latency request_latencies p95 above 60 s for 5 minutes Request latencies Traffic request_count above 10 requests/s for 5 minutes Request count Errors request_count (response_code_class = "5xx" over all) 5xx ratio above 5% for 5 minutes Request count Saturation container/cpu/utilizations, container/memory/utilizations, container/instance_count, container/max_request_concurrencies p99 CPU above 80% for 10 minutes, p99 memory above 80% for 5 minutes, instances above 80% of max_instance_count, or p99 concurrent requests above 80% of max_instance_request_concurrency, each for 5 minutes Container CPU utilization, Container memory utilization, Container instance count, Max concurrent requests Unhealthy instances container/instance_count_with_readiness (readiness_status = "UNHEALTHY"), container/completed_probe_count (is_healthy = false) any instance failing readiness, or any failed probe Container health checks (failed probes: Metrics Explorer)

The traffic policy fires on a spike rather than on silence: an idle environment scaled to zero is normal, while a sustained burst multiplies model spend. The service runs a readiness probe on /health after the startup probe passes, and Cloud Run stops routing requests to an instance that fails it. The unhealthy-instances policy alerts on those readiness failures and on any failed probe. Readiness only starts once startup passes, so the failed-probe condition is what catches a rollout whose new revision never starts while the previous revision keeps serving traffic, which otherwise shows up only as a failed deploy job. /health checks no dependencies, so readiness confirms the process still answers requests.

Dry-run posture: the policies evaluate and open incidents in Cloud Monitoring alerting but notify nobody, so a fork inherits no inbox noise or paging.

Activate notifications: create a notification channel (email, Slack, PagerDuty and others), then add its ID (projects/PROJECT_ID/notificationChannels/CHANNEL_ID) to the environment's list in alert_notification_channels in terraform/main/monitoring.tf. The next deploy attaches it to every policy.

Tune thresholds: alert_thresholds in the same file holds every default. They are starting points for an LLM agent; set them to your own SLOs.

Build from the console: each chart on the Metrics tab has a bell icon that opens the alert builder prefilled with that chart's metric and aggregation, and its View Code button shows the policy JSON. Use it to try a threshold or draft a new policy, then carry the filter and aggregation into monitoring.tf.

docs.title: Callback Logging
docs.text:
LoggingCallbacks (in callbacks.py) logs agent lifecycle events (start/end, model calls, tool invocations) with automatic trace context correlation.

ADK's LoggingPlugin prints a readable trace of every callback to stdout, including user content, outside LOG_LEVEL and the content-capture settings. build_plugins() (in plugins.py) registers it only off Cloud Run: in uv run server, Docker Compose, adk web and the eval lane, locally and in CI. Deployed services rely on LoggingCallbacks for lifecycle, ADK spans and GenAI event records for structure, timing and token usage, and the capture mode for content. A fork deploying outside Cloud Run registers the plugin there too.

docs.title: Gen AI Usage Attributes
docs.text:
ADK records token usage on its generate_content span from GenerateContentResponseUsageMetadata:

Attribute Source fields gen_ai.usage.input_tokens prompt_token_count + tool_use_prompt_token_count gen_ai.usage.output_tokens candidates_token_count + thoughts_token_count gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens cached_content_token_count gen_ai.usage.reasoning.output_tokens thoughts_token_count

For usage analysis over time, use ADK's token metrics (gen_ai.client.token.usage and the adk.experimental.* token histograms) rather than span attributes.

docs.title: Message Content Capture
docs.text:
Two settings decide where user content (prompts, responses, tool arguments and results) lands in OpenTelemetry signals. They do not govern stdout, so LoggingPlugin stays off on Cloud Run and no plugin output reaches deployed logs (Callback Logging):

Setting Controls Default OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT GenAI content: event log records, and the gen_ai.input.messages / gen_ai.output.messages and gen_ai.tool.call.arguments / gen_ai.tool.call.result span attributes Required. Deployed, bootstrap writes it from each root's terraform.tfvars ADK_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT_IN_SPANS Live streaming (/run_live) content on gcp.vertex.agent.data, and content on ADK's deprecated legacy telemetry schema ADK default true, whatever the capture mode

The capture mode takes exactly one of these four values, defined by OpenTelemetry's GenAI utilities:

Value Standard content goes to NO_CONTENT Nowhere (metadata only) EVENT_ONLY GenAI event log records (gen_ai.client.inference.operation.details), shown in the span's Input/Output view in Cloud Trace SPAN_ONLY Span attributes: gen_ai.input.messages and gen_ai.output.messages on model calls, gen_ai.tool.call.arguments and gen_ai.tool.call.result on tool calls SPAN_AND_EVENT Both

Important

NO_CONTENT keeps content out of normal agent runs, but live streaming still records what it sends to the model on gcp.vertex.agent.data unless ADK_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT_IN_SPANS=false. Deployed, Terraform sets it whenever the capture mode is NO_CONTENT; locally, set both in .env.

Captured content raises logging costs and stores user data. The bootstrap examples choose:

  • Dev: SPAN_AND_EVENT. The events feed Cloud Trace's Input/Output view, which reads events, not span attributes. The span attributes put tool arguments and results on the tool spans, the only place they are recorded, and show content in the span attribute panels of Cloud Trace and the ADK web UI. Content is stored twice, and model-call spans grow with the conversation.
  • Stage and prod: NO_CONTENT, so Terraform also sets ADK_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT_IN_SPANS=false and no user content reaches telemetry.
