docs.title: Release a Version
docs.text: Cut releases with release-please, promote them to production, and ship hotfixes.

docs.title: How Releases Work
docs.text:
.github/workflows/release.yml runs release-please on every push to main, using a token from a GitHub App you create once (One-Time Setup).

  • The release pull request: release-please keeps one pull request open, titled like chore(main): release X.Y.Z. It shows the next version and the changelog entries the release will add, and release-please updates it on every push to main. The open pull request takes the place of an [Unreleased] changelog section: to see what the next release contains, open it.
  • The version: release-please reads the Conventional Commits titles merged since the last release. A fix bumps the patch version, a feat the minor version, and a breaking change the major version. Before 1.0.0, a breaking change bumps the minor version instead (bump-minor-pre-major in release-please-config.json).
  • Merging it: release-please tags vX.Y.Z on the squash commit and publishes a GitHub Release with the same notes. The v* tag deploys nothing.
  • The release commit deploys like any merge: it changes pyproject.toml and uv.lock, so it runs the normal merge pipeline (dev in dev-only mode, dev and stage in production mode). That merge run makes the release promotable to prod.
  • uv.lock: release-please bumps version in pyproject.toml but not the project's own entry in uv.lock, which would fail uv sync --locked. An extra-files TOML entry in release-please-config.json bumps that one version line in the same commit, the workaround from release-please#2561. Once release-please#2693 ships, the Python strategy does this itself and the entry can go.

Configuration lives in release-please-config.json (release type, changelog sections, uv.lock entry) and .release-please-manifest.json (the last released version).

docs.title: One-Time Setup (GitHub App)
docs.text:
release-please needs a GitHub App token instead of the default GITHUB_TOKEN: a pull request opened or updated with GITHUB_TOKEN starts no workflow runs, so the release pull request's required checks never report and it can never merge (release-please-action: Other Actions on Release Please PRs). An App token is short-lived and not tied to a person.

Register the App, then store its Client ID and private key, following create-github-app-token: Usage. The template needs these settings:

  1. Repository permissions: Contents, Issues and Pull requests, all Read and write. Metadata sets itself to Read-only. Leave every other permission at No access.
  2. Webhook: uncheck Active. The App only mints tokens.
  3. Installation: choose "Only on this account", create the App, then open Install App and install it on this repository only. Registering the App is not enough: the token request fails until the App is installed.
  4. Variable and secret: store the Client ID (it starts with Iv; the numeric App ID is a different value) and a generated private key under the names release.yml reads: 
    gh variable set RELEASE_APP_CLIENT_ID --body "<client-id>"
gh secret set RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY < <downloaded-key>.pem
    Delete the downloaded .pem file afterwards. GitHub generates a new key whenever you need one.
  5. Immutable releases: enable them in Settings → General → Releases, or run: 
    gh api -X PUT repos/<owner>/<repo>/immutable-releases

Note

Without RELEASE_APP_CLIENT_ID, the release job is skipped. A fork without the App sees no failed runs and gets no releases, so it cuts them by hand: Release Without the App.

docs.title: Release Without the App
docs.text:
Promotion only needs a vX.Y.Z tag on a commit whose merge run deployed stage, so a release can be cut by hand:

  1. In a pull request, set version in pyproject.toml and .release-please-manifest.json, run uv lock, and add the version's entries to CHANGELOG.md. Keeping the manifest current lets release-please continue from this version if you install the App later. The change to pyproject.toml and uv.lock makes the merge run deploy, so the merge commit becomes promotable
  2. Merge it, then tag the merge commit and push the tag. The v* tag deploys nothing: 
    git fetch origin main
git tag -a vX.Y.Z <merge-commit> -m "Release vX.Y.Z"
git push origin vX.Y.Z
  3. In production mode, promote it with the same steps as a release-please release (Promote to Production)

docs.title: Cut a Release
docs.text:
1. Open the release pull request (label autorelease: pending) and review the version and changelog entries
  2. Wait for its required checks, then squash-merge it. The release pull request is generated, so skip editing its title or body: release-please rewrites both on the next push to main
  3. The Release workflow run on the merge commit tags vX.Y.Z, publishes the GitHub Release, and relabels the pull request autorelease: tagged

A merge produces:

  • Tag: vX.Y.Z on the squash commit
  • GitHub Release: immutable, with the version's changelog entries as its notes
  • Changelog: the new version's entries at the top of CHANGELOG.md, and the version in pyproject.toml, uv.lock and .release-please-manifest.json

In dev-only mode, that is the whole release: the merge run deploys the release commit to dev like any other merge.

docs.title: Promote to Production (Production Mode)
docs.text:
Important

The approval gate needs reviewers: set prod_apply_reviewer_users or prod_apply_reviewer_teams in terraform/bootstrap/prod/terraform.tfvars and apply the prod bootstrap root. See Protection Strategies.

A production release is two tags on one commit: vX.Y.Z, which release-please creates when the release pull request merges, and prod-vX.Y.Z, which promotes that commit to prod.

  1. Wait for the release commit's merge run to pass Apply Stage, Smoke Stage and Judge Eval. A promotion pushed earlier fails Require Stage Success and needs a re-run once stage is green
  2. Promote it with a second tag on the same commit (repository admin). Push each promotion tag on its own, since GitHub starts no workflow when more than three tags arrive in one push: 
    git fetch --tags
git tag -a prod-vX.Y.Z 'vX.Y.Z^{commit}' -m "Promote vX.Y.Z to prod"
git push origin prod-vX.Y.Z
    The push starts the prod jobs, and fails at metadata extraction unless the tag has the form prod-vX.Y.Z and vX.Y.Z marks the same commit. Only commits that contain the prod-v* pipeline can be promoted; for an older build, use a Cloud Run traffic split (Rollback).
  3. Monitor the workflow: Actions tab → CI/CD Pipeline
  4. Approved reviewer: Actions → prod-apply job → Review deployments → Approve
  5. Verify the production deployment

docs.title: Hotfix
docs.text:
No GCP access needed. Ship the fix as a new patch release:

  1. Revert or fix on a branch and open a pull request: 
    git checkout -b hotfix/revert-bad-change
git revert --no-edit <bad-commit>
git commit --amend -m "fix: revert <bad change>"
git push origin hotfix/revert-bad-change
gh pr create --title "fix: revert <bad change>"
    Retitle the revert commit: git revert and the GitHub Revert button both title it Revert "...", which is not a Conventional Commit, so release-please skips it and the fix never releases. A one-commit pull request squash-merges under the commit's title, not the pull request's
  2. Merge it after approval. release-please updates the release pull request: a patch version, or a minor version if feat commits are already waiting on main
  3. Merge the release pull request (Cut a Release)
  4. In production mode, promote the new version (Promote to Production)

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
Cloud Run traffic split, instant, requires GCP access:

# List revisions
gcloud run revisions list --service=<service> --region=<region>

# Route all traffic to the previous revision
gcloud run services update-traffic <service> \
  --to-revisions=<previous-revision>=100 \
  --region=<region>

Follow up with a hotfix release. The rollback decision tree is in Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Changelog and Commit Types
docs.text:
release-please writes one changelog entry per commit on main, using its title. You squash-merge, so that is the squash commit title: the PR title by default, or the only commit's title when the pull request has one commit, and whatever the person merging types last. That final title decides the entry, its section and the version bump.

Commit type Changelog section feat Added perf, ci, test Changed revert Removed fix Fixed Any other type (build, docs, chore, refactor, style) Not listed

The mapping is changelog-sections in release-please-config.json; a type it does not list gets no entry. Documentation ships with the change it describes, so that change's entry covers it. When every commit since the last release is unlisted, release-please opens no release pull request.

  • Dependency bumps: Dependabot titles them build(deps), so they are unlisted. When a bump changes what ships, like an ADK upgrade or a security fix, retitle it fix(deps): ... in the squash merge dialog so it gets an entry and a release

  • Breaking changes: a ! after the type or scope (feat!:, feat(api)!:) or a BREAKING CHANGE: footer adds the change to a breaking-changes section at the top of the version's notes, with the footer text as the description. Put the migration steps in that footer

  • Correct a merged entry: edit the merged pull request's body and add a BEGIN_COMMIT_OVERRIDE block with the replacement commit messages, then re-run the latest Release workflow run (Actions tab) to rebuild the release pull request. This also fixes a release pull request whose CHANGELOG.md fails a spelling or whitespace hook because of a typo in a merged title (release-please: How can I fix release notes?)
  • Choose the version: a Release-As: X.Y.Z footer on a commit merged to main makes the next release that version

Note

release-please only adds entries for new versions. Entries for releases before it took over stay as they were written.

docs.title: Immutable Releases
docs.text:
With immutable releases on, a published release's tag cannot be moved or deleted while the release exists. To remove a release and its tag, delete the release first: the tag stays behind, and can then be deleted on its own.

Caution

Deleting a release permanently discards its notes and assets. Once the tag is gone too, a promotion tag for that version fails Extract Build Metadata, since it needs the release tag.

gh release delete vX.Y.Z --yes
gh api -X DELETE repos/<owner>/<repo>/git/refs/tags/vX.Y.Z

← Back to Documentation

docs.title: Template Management
docs.text:
Syncing upstream changes from the template repository.

Tip

First time? Read Setup and Standard Workflow. Quick Reference is your copy-paste guide. Common Patterns and Troubleshooting are optional deep-dives.

docs.title: Philosophy
docs.text:
This template uses transparent git-based syncing rather than opaque automation. You control what updates to pull and when, with full visibility into changes.

Why git sync? - Transparent: Review changes before applying - Selective: Pull only what you need - Flexible: Resolve conflicts your way - No magic: Standard git commands, no proprietary tools

Tip

The /sync-foundation skill (.claude/skills/sync-foundation/SKILL.md) provides an interactive, AI-assisted version of this workflow with phase-ordered review, IDE diffs, and per-file checkpoints.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
One-time configuration:

# Add template repository as foundation remote
git remote add foundation https://github.com/doughayden/agent-foundation.git
git remote -v  # Verify

# Fetch foundation tags to refs/foundation-tags/* (avoids conflicts with local tags)
# --no-tags prevents git from also creating local copies in refs/tags/*
# See: https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Internals-The-Refspec
git fetch foundation 'refs/tags/*:refs/foundation-tags/*' --no-tags

Verify foundation tags were fetched:

# List foundation tags with dates
git for-each-ref refs/foundation-tags --format='%(refname:short) | %(creatordate:short)' --sort=-creatordate

Note

git tag -l only lists refs in refs/tags/*, not custom namespaces. We need git for-each-ref for refs/foundation-tags/*

docs.title: Prepare
docs.text:
Check for updates 

git fetch foundation 'refs/tags/*:refs/foundation-tags/*' --no-tags
git for-each-ref refs/foundation-tags --format='%(refname:short)' --sort=-version:refname | head -10  # Semantic version sort (latest first)

Choose version and set variables 

# Set variables for copy-paste workflow
VERSION=v0.9.1
DOWNSTREAM_PKG=your_agent  # Your package name under src/

# Review what changed
git show foundation-tags/$VERSION:CHANGELOG.md
git log --oneline foundation-tags/v0.9.0..foundation-tags/$VERSION

Create sync branch 

git checkout main && git pull origin main
git checkout -b sync/foundation-$VERSION

docs.title: Sync
docs.text:
Work through each phase in order. See Quick Reference for commands per phase and Common Patterns for detailed git recipes.

Phase Focus Strategy 1 Test fixtures (conftest.py) Sync first — everything else depends on these 2 Code + tests per module IDE diff, adapt code and tests together 3 Bulk test sync Wholesale replacement for unchanged test modules 4 Dependencies & build Manual review (pyproject.toml, Dockerfile, compose.yml) 5 Infrastructure (terraform/) Bulk checkout, verify downstream files preserved 6 CI/CD (.github/workflows/) Bulk checkout, remove foundation-only workflows 7 Config & project files Per-file review (.gitignore, AGENTS.md, tests/AGENTS.md, README.md); terraform/AGENTS.md and .github/workflows/AGENTS.md arrive with phases 5-6 8 Documentation (docs/) Bulk checkout, verify downstream docs preserved 9 Wrap-up Quality suite, summary, PR

docs.title: Test & Merge
docs.text:
# Test thoroughly
uv run pre-commit run --all-files && uv run pytest --cov
docker compose build   # Image still builds; run it with Compose only if .env has the deployed-resource values
terraform -chdir=terraform/bootstrap/dev plan

# Create PR and merge
git push -u origin sync/foundation-$VERSION
gh pr create --title "Sync with foundation template $VERSION"
# Review and merge via GitHub

Tip

To sync unreleased changes from foundation/main, fetch the branch (git fetch foundation main) and replace foundation-tags/$VERSION with foundation/main in commands above.

docs.title: Quick Reference
docs.text:
Commands per phase. Complete Setup and Prepare first to create a branch and set VERSION.

Phase 1 — Test fixtures: 

git diff foundation-tags/$VERSION -- tests/unit/conftest.py
# Adapt fixtures, preserving downstream-only fixtures. No package-name edits needed: the
# conftest derives the package name at runtime, so it diffs clean against upstream.

Phase 2 — Code + tests (per module): 

# Cross-package diff for src/ files: foundation ref path vs your working tree path
git diff foundation-tags/$VERSION:src/agent_foundation/config.py -- src/$DOWNSTREAM_PKG/config.py
# Plain git diff for tests/ paths
git diff foundation-tags/$VERSION -- tests/unit/test_config.py
# Adapt both, preserving downstream-specific code. Repeat for each module.

Phase 3 — Bulk test sync: 

# Check if test module only differs by package name.
# Inner substitution: extract file from ref, replace package name, then diff against local.
diff <(sed "s/agent_foundation/$DOWNSTREAM_PKG/g" <(git show foundation-tags/$VERSION:tests/<file>)) tests/<file>
# If minimal diff: checkout + sed replace. Verify no agent_foundation references remain.

Phase 4 — Dependencies & build: 

git diff foundation-tags/$VERSION -- pyproject.toml
git diff foundation-tags/$VERSION -- Dockerfile compose.yml .env.example
# Manual review and edit. Run uv lock after pyproject.toml changes.

Warning

After syncing pyproject.toml, run uv lock to regenerate lockfile. Never sync uv.lock — CI uses uv sync --locked which fails on stale lockfile.

Phases 5-6 — Infrastructure & CI/CD: 

git checkout foundation-tags/$VERSION -- terraform/
git restore --staged terraform/
git checkout foundation-tags/$VERSION -- .github/workflows/
git restore --staged .github/workflows/
# Verify downstream-specific files preserved. Review with git diff --stat.

Phases 7-8 — Config files & documentation: 

# Per-file review for config
git diff foundation-tags/$VERSION -- .gitignore .dockerignore README.md AGENTS.md tests/AGENTS.md
# Bulk checkout for docs
git checkout foundation-tags/$VERSION -- docs/
git restore --staged docs/

Never bulk sync: - src/ — Your agent implementation (adapt manually in Phase 2) - tests/ — Your test suite (sync fixtures in Phase 1, adapt per-module in Phase 2, bulk sync eligible modules in Phase 3) - CHANGELOG.md — Your version history - .release-please-manifest.json — Your last released version - release-please-config.json — Review per file: keep your package name in package-name and the uv.lock jsonpath, and never copy upstream's bootstrap-sha - init_template.py — Removed from your project after first use - LICENSE — Your project license - uv.lock — Regenerate with uv lock after syncing pyproject.toml

docs.title: Common Patterns
docs.text: Detailed git recipes for the Sync phases.

docs.title: Pull Entire Directory
docs.text:
Warning

Stages all files from foundation version. Overwrites local versions of tracked files in this directory. Untracked local files are not affected. Review with git status before committing.

# Review changes (compares foundation vs current HEAD)
git diff foundation-tags/$VERSION -- docs/

# Sync directory
git checkout foundation-tags/$VERSION -- docs/
git commit -m "docs: sync with foundation $VERSION"

docs.title: Pull Specific File
docs.text:
# Review changes
git diff foundation-tags/$VERSION -- docs/deployment.md

# Sync file
git checkout foundation-tags/$VERSION -- docs/deployment.md
git commit -m "docs: sync deployment.md from $VERSION"

docs.title: Sync a File at a Different Local Path
docs.text:
git checkout requires the same path in both the source and destination. When the foundation uses a different package directory name (e.g., agent_foundation/ vs. your_agent/), use git show to redirect the content instead:

# Review the diff across different paths
git diff foundation-tags/$VERSION:src/agent_foundation/telemetry.py -- src/your_agent/telemetry.py

# Write the foundation version to your local path
git show foundation-tags/$VERSION:src/agent_foundation/telemetry.py > src/your_agent/telemetry.py
git commit -m "chore: sync telemetry.py from foundation $VERSION"

docs.title: Pull Multiple Related Files
docs.text:
# Sync workflows
git checkout foundation-tags/$VERSION -- .github/workflows/
git commit -m "ci: sync workflows from $VERSION"

# Sync Terraform
git checkout foundation-tags/$VERSION -- terraform/bootstrap/
git commit -m "infra: sync bootstrap from $VERSION"

docs.title: Cherry-Pick Specific Commits
docs.text:
# View commits between versions (adjust range as needed)
git log --oneline foundation-tags/v0.9.0..foundation-tags/$VERSION

# Cherry-pick specific commit
git cherry-pick <commit-sha>

# Or: create patch and review
git format-patch -1 <commit-sha>
git apply --check 0001-*.patch  # Test first
git apply 0001-*.patch          # Apply if clean
git commit -m "feat: cherry-pick improvement from $VERSION"

docs.title: Resolve Conflicts
docs.text:
# Attempt sync
git checkout foundation-tags/$VERSION -- docs/deployment.md

# If conflicts occur
git status  # Shows conflicted files

# Resolve manually (look for <<<< ==== >>>>) or use merge tool
git mergetool

# After resolving
git add docs/deployment.md
git commit -m "docs: merge deployment.md from $VERSION"

docs.title: Restore Custom Files
docs.text:
If you accidentally overwrite custom files:

# Sync directory
git checkout foundation-tags/$VERSION -- docs/
git commit -m "docs: sync with $VERSION"

# Restore custom file from previous commit
git checkout HEAD~1 -- docs/custom-tools.md
git commit --amend

docs.title: Add Manual Changes
docs.text:
For heavily customized files (README, AGENTS.md), manually incorporate improvements:

# View upstream changes
git diff foundation-tags/$VERSION -- README.md
git show foundation-tags/$VERSION:README.md  # Or view full file

# Manually edit your file to incorporate useful changes, then commit
git add README.md
git commit -m "docs: incorporate upstream README improvements from $VERSION"

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
# Check for accidental local tag conflicts
git show-ref | grep -E 'refs/tags/(v[0-9])'

# Delete specific local foundation tags (safe - only affects local refs)
git tag -d v0.9.0 v0.9.1

Caution

The following commands delete ALL local tags. Verify remote state before proceeding.

# Reset all local tags to origin
git ls-remote --tags origin  # Verify what you'll restore
git tag -d $(git tag -l)     # Delete all local tags
git fetch origin --tags      # Restore from remote

# Reset foundation-tags namespace (safe - only affects local refs)
git for-each-ref refs/foundation-tags --format='%(refname)' | xargs -n 1 git update-ref -d
git fetch foundation 'refs/tags/*:refs/foundation-tags/*' --no-tags

← Back to Documentation

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Common issues and solutions.

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
Container keeps restarting: 

# Check logs
docker compose logs -f

# Verify .env file
cat .env | grep GOOGLE_

# Ensure gcloud auth configured
gcloud auth application-default login

Changes not appearing: - Code changes: Sync and restart the app within a few seconds via watch mode - Dependency changes: Watch should auto-rebuild - If stuck: Stop and restart with docker compose up --build --watch

IAP tunnel connection failures: - Verify roles/iap.tunnelResourceAccessor is granted on your Google account - Check BASTION_INSTANCE and BASTION_ZONE in .env match deployment outputs - Confirm bastion VM is running: gcloud compute instances describe $BASTION_INSTANCE --zone=$BASTION_ZONE - Check IAP tunnel container logs: docker compose logs iap-tunnel - Verify gcloud config directory is readable: ls -la ~/.config/gcloud/

Permission errors: - App container: Ensure ~/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json exists and is readable - IAP tunnel: Ensure ~/.config/gcloud/ directory is readable (mounted as /gcloud-config via CLOUDSDK_CONFIG)

Port already in use: 

# Check what's using port 8000
lsof -i :8000

# Stop the conflicting process or change PORT in .env
# (Update compose.yml if changing port)

Windows path compatibility: - compose.yml uses ${HOME} (Unix/Mac specific) - Windows users need to update volume paths: - App container ADC: Replace ${HOME}/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json with Windows equivalent - IAP tunnel gcloud config: Replace ${HOME}/.config/gcloud with Windows equivalent - Or use %USERPROFILE% in PowerShell

docs.title: Customized Dockerfile
docs.text:
The shipped Dockerfile never installs the project: it runs the package from /app/src via PYTHONPATH=/app/src (docs/references/dockerfile-strategy.md explains why). Installing the project, like uv's stock Dockerfile does, changes that.

Build fails with failed to open file /app/README.md: - pyproject.toml declares readme = "README.md", so building the project package needs the file - Keep the project uninstalled (uv sync --no-install-project), or copy README.md into the builder before the install step

Web UI or /list-apps shows every installed package as an agent: - Cause: the project is installed and PYTHONPATH no longer points at /app/src, so Python imports the package from .venv/lib/pythonX.Y/site-packages/. server.py derives AGENT_DIR from its own location, which then points ADK at site-packages - Check: docker compose exec app python -c 'import agent_foundation; print(agent_foundation.__file__)' prints a site-packages path - The same cause breaks watch mode: Compose syncs edits to /app/src, but the running code is the installed copy - Fix: restore PYTHONPATH=/app/src (with or without the install, /app/src then comes first on the import path), or set AGENT_DIR=/app/src to fix only the agent listing

docs.title: Direct Execution (uv run server)
docs.text:
Import errors: 

# Reinstall dependencies
uv sync --locked

# Check virtual environment
uv run python -c "import sys; print(sys.prefix)"

Vertex AI authentication failed: 

# Verify gcloud auth
gcloud auth application-default login

# Check project set correctly
gcloud config get-value project

# Verify .env variables
cat .env | grep GOOGLE_

Module not found: 

# Ensure project installed
uv sync --locked

# Verify PYTHONPATH (usually not needed with uv)
uv run python -c "import sys; print(sys.path)"

docs.title: Terraform State Lock
docs.text: See Terraform State Lock in Terraform section below.

docs.title: Workflow Not Triggering
docs.text:
Check path filters: - ci.yml has no path filter, so it runs on every push and pull request; ci-cd.yml and deploy-docs.yml both filter - Only prod-v* promotion tags start ci-cd.yml, and they run regardless of paths. A v* release tag alone starts nothing - GitHub creates no push event for tags when more than three tags arrive in one push (push event), so git push origin --tags with several releases starts nothing. Push each promotion tag on its own - ci-cd.yml filters in two layers: paths-ignore exclusions on the trigger prevent the CI/CD workflow from running on docs or local development changes, and the changes job's deploy and eval filters select which downstream jobs run when the change set passes exclusion. No run at all points at the paths-ignore exclusions; a run where everything after Detect Changes skipped points at the changes job filters. See CI/CD Reference: Path filtering

Verify branch protection: 

# Check branch protection rules
gh api repos/:owner/:repo/branches/main/protection

docs.title: Promotion Tag Fails at Extract Build Metadata
docs.text:
Symptom: a prod-vX.Y.Z run fails in Extract Build Metadata with one of: - Promotion tag <tag> does not have the form <env>-vX.Y.Z: the tag is not a promotion tag for a semantic version, like prod-v1.0 or prod-v1.0.0+build.5. Delete it (repository admin) and push a correctly named one - Promotion tag prod-vX.Y.Z needs release tag vX.Y.Z on the same commit: see the causes below

Cause: the promotion tag names a release tag that does not exist, or that marks a different commit. No prod deploy job starts (Require Stage Success still runs, since it needs only the workflow configuration).

Fix when the release tag is missing: release-please creates vX.Y.Z in the Release workflow run on the release pull request's merge commit. If that pull request merged and the promotion tag marks its merge commit, the run is still in progress or failed (an uninstalled App or a revoked private key): wait for it, or fix the App and re-run it, then use Re-run failed jobs on the failed promotion run.

If the release pull request has not merged, the promotion tag went out before that merge and sits on a commit that will never be the release commit. Leave the release tag to release-please rather than creating it by hand. Delete the promotion tag (repository admin), merge the release pull request, and promote the release commit once its merge run passes stage (Release a Version). 

git push origin :refs/tags/prod-v1.0.1
git tag -d prod-v1.0.1

Fix when releasing without the App: if the promotion tag marks the commit you meant to release, create the release tag there, then use Re-run failed jobs on the failed run. The re-run checks out the repository again and finds the new tag (Release Without the App). 

git tag -a v1.0.1 'prod-v1.0.1^{commit}' -m "Release v1.0.1"
git push origin v1.0.1

Fix when the release tag marks a different commit: the promotion tag is on the wrong commit. Leave the release tag where it is, delete the promotion tag (repository admin), and recreate it on the release commit. Fetch the release tag first: git fetch never overwrites a local tag, so a stale local v1.0.1 would rebuild the same mistake. 

git fetch origin --force tag v1.0.1
git push origin :refs/tags/prod-v1.0.1
git tag -d prod-v1.0.1
git tag -a prod-v1.0.1 'v1.0.1^{commit}' -m "Promote v1.0.1 to prod"
git push origin prod-v1.0.1

docs.title: GCP Auth Rejected or Environment Blocked
docs.text:
Symptom: a job fails in google-github-actions/auth with The given credential is rejected by the attribute condition, or never starts with Branch "<branch>" is not allowed to deploy to <environment> due to environment protection rules.

Cause: each environment's WIF provider accepts only tokens from jobs that declare one of its GitHub Environments, and stage, prod and prod-apply accept only the refs their deployment rules allow (Security Posture Identity Layer).

Fix: add environment: <env> to the job that authenticates. A job on a ref the environment rejects belongs on an allowed ref (main or a prod-v* tag); to allow another ref, add a pattern in the environment's bootstrap root and re-apply it.

docs.title: Startup Failures
docs.text:
Symptom: Cloud Run service won't start, health check timeout

Common causes: - Auth Proxy sidecar crash (Cloud Run restarts automatically, check logs) - VPC egress misconfiguration (Cloud SQL private IP unreachable) - Missing or incorrect environment variables - Credential initialization timeout (~30-60s for first request)

Investigate:

# 1. Check service logs for actual error
gcloud run services logs read <service-name> --region <region> --limit 50

# 2. Test locally with same config
docker compose up --build  # Same image and backends; needs the deployed-resource values in .env

# 3. Verify environment variables set correctly
gcloud run services describe <service-name> --region <region> --format="value(spec.template.spec.containers[0].env)"

docs.title: Cloud SQL Connectivity (Cloud Run)
docs.text:
Symptom: App fails to connect to Cloud SQL, database connection errors in logs

Troubleshoot: 1. Check that roles/cloudsql.client is granted to the app service account 2. Verify Cloud SQL instance is running with private IP enabled 3. Verify Cloud Run direct VPC egress is configured (check vpc_access in Terraform) 4. Check proxy sidecar logs for connection errors: 

gcloud run services logs read <service-name> --region <region> --limit 50
5. If connection timeouts occur under load, upgrade the instance tier in database.tf or enable managed connection pooling (Enterprise Plus edition). See Cloud SQL Scaling

docs.title: Bastion Host Health
docs.text:
Symptom: IAP tunnel connects but database queries fail

Troubleshoot: 1. SSH to bastion via IAP: gcloud compute ssh <bastion-instance> --zone=<zone> --tunnel-through-iap 2. Check Auth Proxy container: docker ps (Container-Optimized OS runs Docker) 3. Check Auth Proxy logs: docker logs $(docker ps -q --filter name=cloud-sql-proxy) 4. Verify bastion SA has roles/cloudsql.client 5. Confirm Cloud SQL instance private IP is reachable from the VPC subnet 6. Check COS iptables allows port 5432: sudo iptables -L INPUT -n | grep 5432 — should show ACCEPT rule. COS default INPUT policy is DROP; the cloud-init runcmd must open port 5432 before starting the proxy. 7. Check proxy listens on all interfaces: sudo ss -tlnp | grep 5432 — should show *:5432 (all interfaces), not 127.0.0.1:5432. The bastion proxy requires --address=0.0.0.0 because IAP tunnel connections arrive from outside the loopback interface. 8. Verify bastion SA can impersonate app SA: the bastion SA needs roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on the app SA (granted via google_service_account_iam_member in Terraform). Without this, --impersonate-service-account fails.

Common error: InvalidAuthorizationSpecificationError: Cloud SQL IAM service account authentication failed — the bastion proxy cannot impersonate the app SA. Verify roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator is granted to the bastion SA on the app SA.

docs.title: ADC quota project and billing errors
docs.text:
Symptom: Terraform fails to read its GCS state with a 403 UserProjectAccountProblem or a billing account error.

The gcloud CLI and Application Default Credentials (ADC) use separate credentials. ADC login can set a quota project from the current gcloud configuration, but changing the CLI project later does not update an existing ADC quota project. A quota project without active billing can cause API requests to fail.

Check that billing is enabled on the intended project and set it as the ADC quota project:

gcloud billing projects describe YOUR_DEV_PROJECT_ID
gcloud auth application-default set-quota-project YOUR_DEV_PROJECT_ID

Setting the quota project requires serviceusage.services.use, included in roles/serviceusage.serviceUsageConsumer. The quota project determines quota and billing attribution for applicable client API requests. It does not enable billing or change where Terraform creates resources. If the error persists, check the state bucket's project and billing status too. See Google Cloud authentication and the ADC quota-project command.

docs.title: State Lock Timeout
docs.text:
# Find who holds the lock
gsutil cat gs://<state-bucket>/main/default.tflock

# If GitHub Actions run is stuck/cancelled, force unlock
terraform -chdir=terraform/main force-unlock <lock-id>

# WARNING: Only force unlock if you're certain no other process is running

docs.title: Plan Drift Detected
docs.text:
Symptom: Terraform plan shows unexpected changes

Common causes: 1. Manual changes in GCP Console 2. Another deployment modified resources 3. Terraform state out of sync

Solutions: 

# 1. Check what changed
terraform -chdir=terraform/main plan

# 2. If manual changes were intentional, import them
terraform -chdir=terraform/main import <resource> <id>

# 3. If drift is unwanted, apply to restore desired state
terraform -chdir=terraform/main apply

docs.title: Environment Variable Not Set
docs.text:
Symptom: Error about missing required environment variable

Check precedence: 1. Environment variables (highest priority) 2. .env file (read by ServerEnv and ADK's agent loader) 3. Default values in code (lowest priority)

Debug: 

# Check .env file
cat .env

# Check environment
env | grep GOOGLE_

# Verify what the server resolves (the environment wins over .env)
uv run python -c "from agent_foundation.config import ServerEnv; print(ServerEnv().google_cloud_project)"

docs.title: Version Conflicts
docs.text:
Symptom: Dependency version errors or import failures

Solutions: 

# Sync dependencies from lockfile
uv sync --locked

# If lockfile stale, regenerate
uv lock

# Update specific package
uv lock --upgrade-package <package-name>

# Nuclear option: delete .venv and reinstall
rm -rf .venv
uv sync --locked

docs.title: Trace/Log Data Not Appearing
docs.text:
Common causes: - OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true in the shell or .env, which turns all export off. Startup still prints the usual telemetry lines, since the SDK, not the template, reads the variable - Wrong project ID or missing authentication - Logs queried under the wrong log name: application logs land in otlp, GenAI events in gen_ai.client.inference.operation.details - Normal delay: Traces and logs take 1-2 minutes to appear in Cloud Console

Debug: 

# Check telemetry settings in .env and the shell
cat .env | grep OTEL_
env | grep OTEL_
cat .env | grep GOOGLE_

# Verify auth
gcloud auth application-default login

# Export errors print to the console; debug logging adds more detail
LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG uv run server

docs.title: Rollback Decision Tree
docs.text:
Production issue detected?
│
├─ App code regression (crashes, errors, bad behavior)
│  │
│  ├─ Have direct GCP prod access?
│  │  └─→ Strategy 1: Cloud Run Traffic Split (instant)
│  │
│  └─ No direct GCP access?
│     └─→ Strategy 2: Hotfix + Release (10-20 minutes)
│
├─ Bad container image (won't start, missing dependencies)
│  │
│  ├─ Old revision exists + have GCP access?
│  │  └─→ Strategy 1: Cloud Run Traffic Split (instant)
│  │
│  └─ No old revision or no GCP access?
│     └─→ Strategy 2: Hotfix + Release (10-20 minutes)
│
├─ Configuration regression (wrong env vars, feature flags)
│  │
│  ├─ Config in GitHub Environment variables?
│  │  └─→ Manual GitHub UI edit + re-trigger deployment
│  │
│  └─ Config in application code?
│     └─→ Strategy 2: Hotfix + Release
│
└─ Infrastructure regression (IAM, GCS, Cloud Run config)
   └─→ Strategy 2: Infrastructure Hotfix + Release

docs.title: Strategy 1: Cloud Run Traffic Split (Instant)
docs.text:
When to use: App code or image regression, have direct GCP access, old revision exists

Steps: 

# List revisions
gcloud run revisions list --service=<service-name> --region=<region>

# Split traffic (instant rollback to previous revision)
gcloud run services update-traffic <service-name> \
  --to-revisions=<previous-revision>=100 \
  --region=<region>

Pros: - Instant rollback (seconds) - No rebuild or redeployment - Can quickly test or roll forward again

Cons: - Requires GCP access - Only works if old revision still exists - Doesn't fix root cause (need follow-up)

docs.title: Strategy 2: Hotfix + Release (10-20 minutes)
docs.text:
When to use: No GCP access, or need to fix config/code permanently

Steps: revert or fix on a branch, merge the PR, then release the fix as a new version (v1.0.1, then prod-v1.0.1 once the merge run's stage jobs pass) and approve the prod-apply job. Commands: Release a Version: Hotfixes and Rollback.

Pros: - Works without GCP access - Fixes root cause (proper git history) - Goes through full CI/CD pipeline (validation)

Cons: - Takes 10-20 minutes - Requires PR approval + prod deployment approval - Slower than traffic split
